maturity: 5 closed trades is an anecdote: the process and risk numbers are the signal, outcome statistics are descriptive only until 30 trades.
headline: Too few closed trades to judge the swing book, options had a strong day, and the real risk to watch is the size of your short option book.

points.label: Swing
points.text: Only five trades have closed this month, and four were losses, but that is too small a sample to conclude anything, and the market has been in an uptrend. Meanwhile the open book looks healthy: most positions are in profit. Today you had two new entry signals (SAGILITY and TORNTPHARM), both bought, and one exit signal on ASHOKLEY. You cannot yet say whether you are getting better, because there is no earlier month to compare with.

points.label: Options
points.text: Ten option contracts closed today and eight made money, Rs9,126 in total. The best came from VMM, ENRIN and KEI, and the two losers were NATIONALUM and NMDC. That is a good day, but it is still a small sample: with a 3x stop you need to win about 77% of the time to break even, so judge the strategy after roughly 30 trades. Volatility is on the high side (India VIX about 17.7), which means decent premiums. Stocks with rich premiums and no position right now are CROMPTON, YESBANK and IRFC. It's too early to name favourites, but NATIONALUM has cost you the most so far.

points.label: Events
points.text: Almost nothing is due in the next three weeks: only PFC goes ex-dividend today, and you have no option positions on it. None of your open options runs through a results or dividend date. The busy period is coming: January and February bring a large number of results across your stocks, and you hold over a hundred short options. Before then, work out which ones expire after their stock's results date, and plan to close them beforehand.

points.label: Risk management
points.text: You passed 5 of 6 discipline checks. The one miss is the ASHOKLEY put spread, which is against a red trend, so close it at tomorrow's open. Financial Services is now almost half of your capital, well above your 40% limit, so avoid adding more. Your options are the biggest risk: a 5% market fall would cost over 5% of capital, and a sharp one with higher volatility could cost more than 17%, mostly because 36 stocks carry naked short calls. If every swing position hit its Supertrend exit today, you would lose Rs60,780. From 30 November you will no longer average losers; they go to the exit line.

action: Close the ASHOKLEY put spread in Kite at tomorrow's open, and keep new Financial Services positions inside the 40% limit.
